solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's manufactured with poor cuts? On the contrary

definitions.text: It's manufactured with poor cuts? On the contrary

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up from raw materials, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the IT of It's is taken as written; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: A sniffy remark that some cured meat is made from inferior offcuts, promptly retracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the statement: the ham is not made from poor cuts; rather the words themselves, reworked, make the ham. The whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosciutto is Italian dry-cured ham, sold in thin slices, so cuts of meat are its very substance.

clue.text: Like a gag, perhaps, to chastise

parts.note: a gag is a joke, of which a pun is one kind
the suffix -ish means like, as in boyish

explanation.surface: A gag as a means of punishment, a brutal way to silence someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gag' suggests something stuffed in the mouth, but it is a joke; 'Like a pun' gives PUN-ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To punish someone is to discipline them for wrongdoing, a straight synonym of chastise.

clue.text: Like a gag, perhaps, but covering top of eyes

indicators.note: covering the top hides the first letter, so it drops out

parts.note: jocular means joking, like a gag

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue: a gag that also blindfolds its victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a gag' repeats the last clue's opening but now gives JOCULAR, whose top letter J is concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eye or to sight, as in ocular muscles.

clue.text: 'Little Britain' vicar, struggling with clues, aspires to be one?

definitions.text: 'Little Britain' vicar, struggling with clues, aspires to be one?

indicators.note: struggling suggests something twisting about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: little means shortened, so Britain is cut down to Brit

explanation.surface: A comedy-show clergyman wrestling with a crossword, keen to master it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Britain' is a TV sketch show, but here it just means Britain shortened. The clue as a whole describes the answer, a semi-all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruciverbalist is a crossword enthusiast, setter or solver, the role a puzzled vicar might aim at.

clue.text: Failing to focus on target, world body expressed regret — about time!

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is the world body

indicators.note: about means the sighing word goes round the letter for time

parts.note: sighed means let out a regretful breath

explanation.surface: The United Nations, having failed to act, finally voices regret after much delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unsighted means being unable to see, so one cannot aim at a mark.

clue.text: Fish caught by Muscovite trawler

indicators.note: caught by means the fish sits held within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A Russian fishing boat lands a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: This is oddly coloured

indicators.note: oddly means take the letters in the odd-numbered places (first, third, fifth, seventh) of coloured

explanation.surface: A remark that something looks strangely tinted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the very thing the solver is reading, a self-referential definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The words in front of the solver form a crossword clue, so 'This' names one by pointing at itself.

clue.text: Acted like a chicken, going like this with arms — surrendered

parts.note: a hen lays eggs, so a chicken laid
this clue runs down the grid, so going like this means down

explanation.surface: A cowardly soldier, chicken by nature, throwing down weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' suggests cowardice, but the bird simply lays eggs. 'going like this' refers to the clue's own direction in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay down one's arms is the idiom for giving up the fight.

clue.text: It's good to see Radio One's able to cover outskirts of Derby

indicators.note: radio means words heard over the air, so a word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: one can be I, the first person, or the Roman numeral
can means is able

indicators.note: outskirts of takes the outer letters of Derby, its first and last

explanation.surface: A radio station claims it can broadcast to the area around Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radio One' looks like the BBC station, but 'Radio' makes I heard as EYE. Derby is an English city in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is something visually attractive but not substantial, pleasant to look at.

clue.text: Ingredient for making rock — mix it with treacle and put in three parts of rice and two of gum

indicators.note: mix means stir the pieces together into a fresh order
three parts of takes the first three letters of rice
two of takes the first two letters of gum

explanation.surface: A recipe for a sticky confection: treacle, rice and gum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests the British seaside sweet, but it is rock music. 'put in' just adds the letters to the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock music is built around the sound of amplified guitars, a core part of the band.

clue.text: State between Argentina and Uruguay

indicators.note: between points to the letters at the junction of the two country names, the end of one running into the start of the other

explanation.surface: A geography question about a country lying between two South American neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' keeps only the letters where the two names meet, the tail of the first and the head of the second; 'and' just joins them. The surface tempts a map search, but the island is in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny independent island republic in the south-west Pacific, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Special reservists in retreat loudly fired revolver …

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the reservists' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: loudly says the word for fired is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: fired, set burning, means alight

explanation.surface: A tale of soldiers in a hasty withdrawal firing a handgun noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' looks like a gun to go with 'fired', but it is something that revolves in orbit. 'loudly' makes ALIGHT sound like the last syllables ELLITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite revolves around a planet, so it is a thing that goes round and round in orbit.

clue.text: … refusing to kill in half-hearted combat

indicators.note: half-hearted means the doubled letter at the heart of the word loses one of its pair

parts.note: sparring is practice fighting, as in boxing

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: a fighter holding back from finishing off an opponent in a lacklustre bout.
explanation.walkthrough: SPARRING has RR at its centre; 'half-hearted' halves that pair, leaving one R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparing an enemy means showing mercy and letting them live.

clue.text: Song with villain invading idyllic land

indicators.note: invading means the villain's letters break into the middle of the song's

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter

explanation.surface: An operatic story of a villain bursting into a pastoral paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia, a region of ancient Greece, became the poetic byword for an unspoilt rural paradise.

clue.text: Former PM, getting a tip-off after bug planted by journalist, bristled greatly over watchers

indicators.note: after puts the former PM's letters following the bug's
planted by puts the journalist's letters right up against what comes before

parts.note: a beetle is an insect, loosely a bug

indicators.note: getting a tip-off means the name loses its final letter, its tip

parts.note: Gordon Brown was a UK Prime Minister
ED is the usual crossword abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A spy-thriller scene: a former Prime Minister tipped off about a listening device planted by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests a hidden microphone, but it is an insect. The definition describes thick bushy brows sitting over the eyes ('watchers').
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with heavy, overhanging, shaggy eyebrows is said to be beetle-browed; 'watchers' are the eyes beneath.

clue.text: Shock of Frenchman turning up with sailor after spending a penny

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: René is a common French man's name

indicators.note: after spending means the sailor's letters lose the coin, as if paid out

parts.note: Popeye is the cartoon sailor man
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A French man is taken aback when he meets a sailor after using a public toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spending a penny' is British slang for using the toilet, but here it means losing a P (penny). The sailor loses his second P, giving POEYE, and 'turning up' reverses the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation that startles someone opens their eyes to the truth.

clue.text: Lawyer picking up chap pointlessly during a night out

indicators.note: during means the chap's letters go inside those of the outing

parts.note: a date is a night out together

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up means raising the letters, so they read upwards
pointlessly means losing a compass point, here east

parts.note: cove is old slang for a chap or fellow

explanation.surface: A lawyer collects a guy aimlessly on an evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' suggests collecting someone on a date, but it is the reversal. COV turned upward gives VOC.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate is a barrister or lawyer who pleads cases in court.

clue.text: Respected editor held up ending of 'Close Encounters'

indicators.note: held means the editor's letters hold the others inside them
in a down clue up means the enclosed letters read from the bottom
ending of takes the last letter of Close

parts.note: meets means encounters

explanation.surface: An editor delays the finale of a famous science-fiction film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close Encounters' looks like the Spielberg film title, but it splits in two; 'up' turns E plus the encounters word to STEEME, which 'held' puts inside the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed means held in high regard, admired.

clue.text: I bend codes dreadfully — that is, essentially, ____

definitions.text: I bend codes dreadfully — that is, essentially, ____

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests things done badly, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: i.e., short for id est, is the essential written form of that is

explanation.surface: A rule-breaker confesses to bending the codes, inviting the solver to fill in the word for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank asks the solver to supply the word the confession describes; the whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bending codes badly means failing to obey rules, which is refusal to comply.

clue.text: In a hole, SA President's not one to break promise on housing

indicators.note: In means the trimmed president goes inside the hole

parts.note: a gap is a hole

indicators.note: not one means a letter standing for one, the a, is dropped

parts.note: Jacob Zuma was President of South Africa

explanation.surface: A beleaguered South African president who is not one to go back on his word.
explanation.walkthrough: Gazumping is a British property practice: a seller accepts a higher offer after agreeing a price with someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To gazump is to back out of an agreed house sale for a bigger offer.

clue.text: More than one star born in just over half of the sky

indicators.note: in means the born letter goes inside the shortened sky word
just over half of keeps five of the nine letters, dropping the rest

parts.note: celestial means of the sky or heavens

explanation.surface: A star born in the heavens, astronomically speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests astronomy, but it is a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebs, short for celebrities, are famous people, stars of screen or stage.

clue.text: Romantic monologue beginning more than halfway through, one part covering another

indicators.note: the first letter, the beginning, is shifted to a spot more than half way along

parts.note: love, the romantic sort, as in a love song
a rap is a spoken-word piece by one performer

explanation.surface: A romantic speech that begins only after it is mostly over, with one element obscuring another.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of LOVERAP moves from the front to fifth of seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: When things overlap, part of one lies on top of part of the other.

clue.text: Formal start to overture — first part in piece

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal or proper

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of overture

explanation.surface: A stiff, formal opening to a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the primo is the upper part, the first of the two players.

clue.text: Fruit being ripe, should it be plucked before eating?

definitions.text: should it be plucked before eating?

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit
to age is to mature or ripen

explanation.surface: A kitchen question about whether ripe fruit should be picked before it is eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plucked' seems to mean picking the fruit; it is pulling feathers from a fowl before it is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's feathers are plucked out before the bird is cooked and eaten.

clue.text: E.g. I dabbled with sadism — no?

definitions.text: E.g. I dabbled with sadism — no?

indicators.note: dabbled suggests splashing about and stirring, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An awkward confession of a past flirtation with cruelty, half-hoping to be contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: The statement 'I dabbled with sadism' is itself an example of the answer, and its letters with NO make it.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning up to a past misdeed, such as a dalliance with cruelty, is a confession.

clue.text: Brown, at heart, perpetually perplexed

indicators.note: perplexed means confused, so the central letters are jumbled
at heart takes the central letters of perpetually, dropping its outer stretches

explanation.surface: Someone named Brown who is permanently baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname but is the colour. The heart of perpetually is PETUA, five letters that rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Taupe is a brownish grey shade, named after the French word for mole.

clue.text: He'll make the drink go round

definitions.text: He'll make the drink go round

parts.words: He'll make the drink go round
parts.note: 'He' suggests a host sharing beverages, but the drink is the sea and the swirl is water turning; the answer is also a man's name

explanation.surface: A generous host who ensures everyone gets a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, and 'He' fits because the answer is also a man's name, short for Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool or circular current makes water spin round, and the same letters form a man's name.

clue.text: Rejecting the unattainable, hence encourages accepting average return

parts.note: hence, therefore, means so

indicators.note: accepting means the spurring word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: urges means encourages or spurs on

indicators.note: return means the word for average comes back reversed

parts.note: par is the standard or average

explanation.surface: Advice that encouragement and modest returns are the way to come to terms with failure.
explanation.walkthrough: From Aesop's fox, who decided the grapes it could not reach were sour anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour grapes is disparaging what one cannot get, pretending not to want it.
